# P2a final scoped performance review: current component and SDK evidence

**PASS within the owner component/SDK review scope.** No blocking performance
finding is established by the current source or these fixture runs. Source is
`7e3f72ebfaef39d6e6630dd11fa7dc91c8985d4a`, with 4,743 verified source hashes and
digest `d64467aee29afb00a1a009cf94cdcdad10600160fc529dfcf3c91e9648e064f1`.
This verdict excludes Root full-app, native, full-CI and exact-reference capture
gates. It does not mark the IDE or this phase complete.

## Evidence checked independently, without rerunning tools

Verified current source paths/hashes, clean status and tracked index, and every
before/after source guard for the five normal component gates. Verified exact
raw-log hashes and actual test-result lines: 291 all-feature tooling tests pass
with zero failed, ignored or filtered; default UI has 125 passed, zero failed,
one inherited ignored test and zero filtered. Normal all-feature library build,
strict repository Clippy and workspace formatting pass. Recorded command wall
seconds are 7.509 for the library, 17.778 for tooling tests, 10.111 for Clippy,
28.925 for formatting and 132.509 for the UI command including its build. These
are verification-command durations, not IDE startup or feature benchmarks.

Compiler JSON contains the current absolute library source path and a fresh
compilation. Its recorded normal library is SHA-256
`9c8c3235cac1fcfc10832e8af791487865164786533fb45afecac2440d0be570`.
The release receipt and SDK probe build bind that library to this source; exact
probe source/binary hashes and all three actual typed-decoder outputs verify.
No giant artifact copy or runtime rerun was required by this review. The shared
Cargo cache path is mutable; the checked historical compilation receipts provide
the source binding, rather than a promise that the path remains immutable later.

## SDK capture size and timing evidence

| Scenario | Projects / Basic modules | Prior record bytes | Current record bytes | Current total stdout bytes | Current command seconds |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| baseline | 3 / 2 | 227,184 | 233,461 | 235,652 | 9.958 |
| nested | 7 / 4 | 228,673 | 241,770 | 244,048 | 10.294 |
| late | 7 / 4 | 228,673 | 241,789 | 244,209 | 9.732 |


All eight actual commands were checked: six successful captures form three
prior/current pairs, and two exit-1 captures correctly reject included builds
without publishing a model. Supported-pair comparisons preserve the entire Basic
and V2 envelope, nested property order and list order after removing only
`importFacts`; no path or value normalization is applied. Each private input
manifest is unchanged across its command. The actual Rust probes decode Basic,
V2 and identity facts and verify current model/selection bindings. The late Idea
name equals the independent official getter oracle after project-evaluation
callbacks, with its raw oracle line retained.

Both accepted records and complete captured stdout are below the existing
16 MiB bound in these fixtures. The largest current record is 241,789 bytes.
These are small three- and seven-project catalogues, not a large-project test.
Commands use sequential fixture runs with `--no-daemon`; prior runs populate
build/filesystem caches. No controlled repetitions, cold-start comparison or
speedup conclusion follows from the observed command durations. The typed probe
process durations likewise are fixture execution evidence, not IDE latency.

The runtime tuple is supplementary JDK 21, Gradle 9.6.1, AGP 9.4.0 and SDK 37.
Only the private validation modules explicitly select installed build-tools
37.0.0. The earlier two complete records with unavailable build-tools-36.0.0 V2
facts remain preserved; their Gradle commands exited zero but they did not earn
successful V2-decoder credit. No SDK install/license, original reference fixture,
source expectation or test assertion was changed to obtain the successful runs.
The official Gradle/AGP/JVM and minimal getter serialization remain the documented
external-runtime exception; Rust owns validation and import policy.

## Source performance assessment and remaining measurements

The previous independent static findings carry forward. Catalogue order stays
in a vector, while a `BTreeMap` supports duplicates, parent checks and Basic
module matching in O(P log P + M log P) comparisons plus field-byte validation.
Getter bodies add no production task, task dependency, dependency resolution,
Provider realization or new Gradle invocation. Parallel policy remains a bounded
pure decision with no scheduler or new production caller.

Selection validation includes selected-module variant scans. Freshness checks
reconstruct owned Basic identities when revisions/selections match, with cost
proportional to those identities. Canonical-path getters perform filesystem work
and root directory observations repeat per project. Those costs remain explicit;
this task has not introduced a frequent render-loop identity caller.

The 16 MiB decoder acceptance limit bounds the input before Rust JSON allocation;
it is not a 16 MiB peak-heap guarantee. Catalogue maps, typed fields and identity
copies require additional memory. JVM maps and full JSON are constructed before
Rust rejects an oversized record, so the producer heap remains unbounded by that
acceptance check. The additive sidecar shares the existing total stdout budget
with Basic/V2 data and other output. These small real captures establish usable
headroom here, not capacity for arbitrary projects. Representative large-project
capture duration, peak memory, cancellation responsiveness and future publication
call frequency remain to be measured. No IDE startup, RSS, hardware rendering,
large-project pass or measured improvement is claimed.

## Preserved failures and scope limits

Three semantic product fix rounds, the separately recorded nonsemantic clone
cleanup and the prior user-facing escalation remain preserved. Earlier actual
Clippy/independent quality FAIL evidence is hash-bound and retains its original
verdict; the corrected current Clippy pass is a separate execution. The initial
current-source ENOSPC log/exit and the successful capacity-retry logs remain
separate; cache recovery did not change production source or assertions. Prior
static reviews and SDK failure records were not overwritten.

This review introduces no test removal, skip, weakened assertion, semantic fix
round or original-test parity credit. Naming, Kotlin/facet and generated-tree
reference tests remain applicable and unported. No Cargo, rustc, JVM, Gradle,
application, native, cache or Git mutation was run by this reviewer; only the two
external final review files were created. Root full-app/native/full-CI and exact
reference captures remain distinct lead gates.
